newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: RESEARCH ALERT-Ceylon Tobacco a buy-UBS.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Ceylon Tobacco a buy-UBS.

text.p: UBS Keells has issued a "buy" rating on Sri Lankan blue chip Ceylon Tobacco Company Ltd, saying volume growth, cost rationalisation, reduced interest and corporate tax will lift the company's earnings.
"Although the stock moved up 22 percent since the beginning of April 1997, it is still relatively cheap," it said in a report seen by Reuters on Tuesday.
The share last traded at 46 rupees on Monday.
CTC, the only producer of cigarettes in Sri Lanka, should benefit from annual volume growth of 1.6 percent expected over the next three years, said the report.
Ceylon Tobacco, a subsidiary of B.A.T. Industries Plc , is the main supplier of cigarettes in Sri Lanka where the market was around 5.5 billion sticks in 1996.

The company began rationalising cost in 1996 by investing 212 million rupees in state-of-the-art equipment, which helped to improve productivity by 26 percent, said the report. "Further investments of 200 millioin rupees per annum to improve productivity are planned for 1997-1999."
CTC's effective tax rate is seen easing due to the firm being eligible for investment relief on capital investments made since 1996.
"Given falling interest rates, we expect interest exposure to reduce in the future," the report said.
Interest rates have eased due to improved money supply after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios of commercial banks by three percent this year.
The report says net profit forecasts for 1997, 1998 and 1999 are 645 million rupees, 725 and 821.
The company reported a net profit of 575 million rupees for the financial year ended 31 December, 1996.
